text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Zeroual meets Colombian President Samper to discuss cooperation. Trade between the two countries was worth $18 million in 1996.
- Some 7,740 candidates stand for June 5 parliamentary elections. More than 30 political parties field candidates for 380-seat National Assembly; 68 contenders run as independents.
- Political parties step up preparations for campaign to start on May 15.
- Algeria commemorates massacre of thousands of civilians by colonial French troops on May 8, 1945, in eastern Algeria.
- Management of iron and steel firm Sider agrees with workers' union on restructuring plan.
- Government vows to crack down on fiscal fraud and tax evasion. Authorities increased direct tax collecting by 59.5 percent to 36.7 billion dinars ($658 million) in 1996 from 23 billion in 1995.
- Most political parties hope June 5 elections will help restore peace. Authorities give total of 99 hours airtime for all candidates to broadcast on state-run radio and television.
